author: PT-dove
policy: Every text under licenses/ exists because it was fetched from an upstream source that publishes it. The build re-hashes each file against the digest recorded here and fails on any mismatch, so a text cannot be swapped without editing this record. Nothing here is reconstructed, paraphrased or inferred: a missing text stays an open gap (see manifests/license-gaps.json).

verification: The downloaded archive digest equals the line published in the official SHASUMS256.txt for v24.20.0.
node.exe inside that archive has the same SHA-256 as runtime/node/node.exe in every bundle built from it, so the text and the binary come from one release artifact.

The same text also exists at raw.githubusercontent.com/nodejs/node/v24.20.0/LICENSE; that copy is byte-identical after normalising the archive's CRLF line endings (157609 vs 160555 bytes = +1 byte per line).
node.note: The Windows installer in C:\Program Files\nodejs ships no LICENSE file, which is why the text has to come from the release archive rather than from the machine that provides node.exe.

packages.name: @deepseek-ai/dsh-experimental-inspector
packages.sourcePath: LICENSE at the repository root; the package manifest declares repository.directory = packages/experimental/inspector
verification: The tag dsh-v0.2.2-alpha.2 is the release this version was published from (registry dist-tag history and the repository tag list agree).
The published tarball ships no license text of its own; lib/devtools/LICENSE inside it is the bundled Chromium DevTools notice, which is a different work and was NOT used as this package's license.

packages.name: @koromix/koffi-win32-x64
packages.sourcePath: package/LICENSE.txt in the koffi@3.1.1 tarball (the platform packages are split out of this release and omit the text)
verification: The platform package @koromix/koffi-win32-x64@3.1.1 and koffi@3.1.1 are one release: the platform package is a binary carrier for the same version and its manifest points at github.com/Koromix/koffi.
The platform tarball contains only index.js, package.json, win32_x64/koffi.lib, win32_x64/koffi.node and README.md, so the release-level LICENSE.txt is the authoritative text.

unobtainable.name: dfa
unobtainable.reason: Upstream publishes no license text at all: not in any published tarball, not in the repository at the published commit, not on the default branch.
evidence: registry tarball dfa-1.2.0.tgz contains only package.json, compile.js(.map), index.js(.map) and README.md — no LICENSE/COPYING/NOTICE.
registry tarball dfa-2.0.0.tgz likewise contains no license file, so this is not a packaging accident of one version.

github.com/devongovett/dfa redirects to github.com/foliojs/dfa; the tree at gitHead 3f5e603e5082caedabefefdf53e8a6ca3111e966 and the default branch both list no LICENSE, and the commit history for path LICENSE is empty.
The only licence statement upstream makes is the package.json field "license": "MIT" plus "author": "Devon Govett <devongovett@gmail.com>".
unobtainable.decision: Closed by removal, not by reconstruction. No text was ever generated for this package, because a copyright line cannot be reconstructed from a package.json field without inventing an attribution the upstream never wrote. M8-DFA-PRUNE then removed dfa@1.2.0 from the distribution entirely (it is unreachable from the mounted profile), so the obligation to ship its text no longer applies to this bundle; `status` stays `open` because the upstream text still does not exist and this record must not imply it was obtained.
